title: The Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary
short_summary: The Queenship of the Blessed Virgin Mary is a Marian memorial, instituted by Pope Pius XII, that honors Mary's unique and entirely dependent share in the kingship of her Son.
key_facts: The U.S. calendar keeps this memorial on August 22, in the octave of the Assumption.
Pope Pius XII instituted the feast in 1954 through the encyclical Ad Caeli Reginam.
The 1969 calendar reform moved the observance to August 22 to link it with the Assumption.
Mary's queenship flows entirely from her Son's kingship and her unique share in his saving work.

sections.heading: Instituted by Pius XII
sections.body: Pope Pius XII established this memorial in 1954 with the encyclical Ad Caeli Reginam, teaching that Mary shares in a unique way in the kingship of her Son because of her role as Mother of God and her cooperation in the work of redemption.

sections.heading: Placed after the Assumption
sections.body: When the liturgical calendar was reformed after the Second Vatican Council, this memorial was moved to August 22, placing it within the octave of the Assumption so that Mary's queenship is understood in close connection with her bodily glorification.

sections.heading: A queenship entirely dependent on Christ
sections.body: The doctrine of Mary's queenship does not place her alongside Christ as an equal ruler. Her queenship is a created share in her Son's kingship, granted by grace, and is always understood as wholly dependent on him.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Christ the King, Mary the Queen Mother
catholic_connection_sections.body: Catholic teaching presents Mary's queenship on the pattern of the queen mother in the biblical kingdom of David, whose honor comes entirely from her son the king.

catholic_connection_sections.heading: Devotion ordered to Christ
catholic_connection_sections.body: As with all Marian doctrine, this memorial is meant to lead the faithful more deeply toward Christ, not to obscure his unique kingship.
